# MAIW browser workspace reference

| V3 fields | NAND mapping and export boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Session ID, title, timestamps, pin and workspace panels | Local task ID plus original source ID/fingerprint; title and pin remain editable. Original layout and official panel URLs stay in provenance for v3 export. No local account is inferred. |
| Turn ID, parent session, sequence, prompt and optional question | Local round identity and task relation; original sequence, question presence and combined prompt are retained. |
| Applied template ID/name/content/order | Frozen round snapshots plus original ID/order; no independent library or upstream revision is invented. |
| Exchange IDs, parents, panel/provider and target index | Local answer and historical target relation, including panels removed from the current workspace. |
| Response text/Markdown, statuses, timestamps and capture metadata | Separate imported transcript sections and source metadata. No native receipt, verified capture or website identity is created. |
| Native NAND export | Supported v3 projection of selected tasks and current answers; unsupported state, runtime data and prior capture revisions stay outside the format. |

History migration references the pinned `src/db/history-transfer.ts`, `database.ts`, `session-service.ts` and history-transfer tests. They map to NAND's `core/workspace/maiw-format.ts`, `history-transfer.ts`, `imported.ts` and tests. `scripts/generate-maiw-history-fixture.mjs` runs the actual pinned export function against deterministic in-memory database rows; it does not claim an extension UI export or real account session. NAND adds source fingerprints, explicit conflict previews, Markdown persistence and separate imported transcript provenance. Imported completion never becomes a verified NAND capture. V3 omits full acquisition snapshots, independent prompt libraries and template revisions; its one-current-panel-per-provider limit is documented in the [migration guide](../browser.md#ai-workspace). Unsupported fields and relationships are rejected before writes; unrepresentable exports are rejected without truncation.

`core/providers/quality.ts` uses the empty/title/status-only categories from the pinned upstream's `src/core/acquisition/quality-gate.ts`. It does not infer completeness from text length. Confirmed titles are bounded projections from supported history responses; branch and terminal evidence remain separate requirements. Capture comparison uses explicit immutable revision IDs, following the newest-partial principle documented in upstream `src/db/acquisition-snapshot-service.ts`. NAND uses its existing Markdown store rather than importing Dexie or extension runtime hooks.

NAND adapts DeepSeek, Kimi, ChatGPT, Claude and Qwen history parsing from [MAIW](https://github.com/NAMEWTA/multi-ai-browser-extension/tree/b6b83ca90f0f67fbf25a676e7a8f6b8b34327800), pinned to commit `b6b83ca90f0f67fbf25a676e7a8f6b8b34327800`. The upstream is MIT licensed, Copyright (c) 2026 NAMEWTA. Its [license](maiw-LICENSE.txt) is preserved and its attribution is included in [NOTICE](../../NOTICE).

| Upstream source | NAND implementation | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/providers/deepseek/acquisition.ts` and its legacy/fragment fixtures | `src/modules/browser/core/providers/deepseek-history.ts` | History envelopes, public request/response fragments, stable message IDs and parent-chain traversal |
| `src/providers/deepseek/runtime-acquisition.ts` | Same parser's endpoint allowlist | Exact DeepSeek origin, history endpoint and conversation parameter |
| `src/providers/deepseek/selectors.ts`, `strategy.ts` and `native-copy.ts` | `src/modules/browser/platform/desktop/deepseek-dom.ts` | Composer/submit/new-chat selectors, shared send/stop control detection and exclusions for scoped answer DOM |

Kimi additionally uses the same pinned upstream's `src/providers/kimi/acquisition.ts`, `runtime-acquisition.ts` and two list-messages fixtures in `src/modules/browser/core/providers/kimi-history.ts`. Its selectors and scoped-content exclusions are mapped to `platform/desktop/kimi-dom.ts`. Only conversation identity and pagination cursor are projected from the allowlisted POST body. Pagination follows observed requests; it never replays them.

NAND rejects missing or duplicate message IDs instead of inventing identities from array positions. It preserves repeated text fragments, excludes reasoning/tool/status fragments, checks declared conversation identity and retains explicit reasons for incomplete branch or pagination evidence. Parsing a history response does not prove that an answer finished generating. Kimi requires an explicit terminal status; a status ending with “unfinished” is not completion evidence.

ChatGPT uses the pinned `src/providers/chatgpt/acquisition.ts`, its current-branch test, `runtime-acquisition.ts`, `selectors.ts` and `native-copy.ts` as references for `core/providers/chatgpt-history.ts` and `platform/desktop/chatgpt-dom.ts`. The mapping/current-node structure supplies explicit ancestry; only public messages on that branch are projected. NAND additionally requires terminal status and end-turn evidence, preserves repeated parts and excludes non-public channels. Numbered turn containers never become message identities.

Claude uses the pinned `src/providers/claude/acquisition.ts`, `runtime-acquisition.ts`, `selectors.ts` and `native-copy.ts` as references for `core/providers/claude-history.ts` and `platform/desktop/claude-dom.ts`. NAND retains repeated public text blocks and requires explicit parent edges, an active message tip and end-turn evidence. The last assistant message alone does not prove completeness. Role labels and array positions never become message IDs. Missing evidence remains partial; local fixtures do not verify the current private website schema.

Qwen uses the pinned `src/providers/qwen/acquisition.ts`, detail/alternate/partial fixtures, `runtime-acquisition.ts`, `selectors.ts`, `strategy.ts` and `native-copy.ts` for `core/providers/qwen-history.ts` and `platform/desktop/qwen-dom.ts`. NAND keeps repeated fragments and reports ambiguous progressive prefixes without choosing the longest text. Missing parent fields do not establish a root. Explicit pagination, active branch and terminal evidence are required. The composer excludes conversation search and verification controls; empty Slate placeholders and dormant verification containers supply no draft or challenge evidence.

Doubao maps the pinned `src/providers/doubao/acquisition.ts`, two chain-page fixtures, `runtime-acquisition.ts`, `selectors.ts`, `strategy.ts` and `native-copy.ts` to `core/providers/doubao-history.ts` and `platform/desktop/doubao-dom.ts`. NAND joins only observed cursor chains, preserves repeated public blocks and requires stable message IDs, explicit roots and terminal status. Exhausted pagination alone does not establish ancestry or generation completion. It does not synthesize IDs, choose the longest conflicting answer or replay requests. The original reference fixtures omit root/terminal evidence and therefore remain partial under this stricter contract.

The passive response observer in `platform/desktop/provider-responses.ts` is written for NAND. Each task owns its observation lifetime, uses the existing guest operation queue, retains only projected message data and drops late results after cancellation or guest replacement. It does not replay credentials or fetch website APIs independently.

Coze's pinned `definition.ts`, `selectors.ts`, `strategy.ts`, `native-copy.ts` and scoped-copy test map to `platform/desktop/coze-dom.ts`, `scoped-chat-dom.ts` and `coze-session.ts`. The reference has no API acquisition adapter. NAND installs no response observer for this policy, binds one exact official host for each session and requires explicit public conversation/message/parent attributes. Test IDs and DOM positions do not become message identities. Scoped DOM and website-copy results remain partial. An unproved permalink is not synthesized; source reveal uses only the original captured page generation and validates the saved message identity.

MiniMax's corresponding six pinned files map to `minimax-dom.ts`, the shared `scoped-chat-dom.ts` and `minimax-session.ts`. Its user/assistant class selectors remain specific to MiniMax, while identity, content and copy checks share the same contract. No API strategy exists in this reference. The allowlist also includes `agent.minimax.cn`, the destination observed when opening the official `chat.minimax.io` entry on October 11, 2026. That public redirect establishes an entry point, not authenticated DOM or permalink compatibility.

The pinned `src/entrypoints/native-copy-main.content.ts` and `src/runtime/native-copy-client.ts` informed the copy-boundary review. NAND's `platform/desktop/provider-copy.ts` uses a narrower synchronous dispatch contract: one explicit public-answer control, no transient user activation, bounded Clipboard payloads, blocked legacy copy/cut and restored methods. Production guest permissions deny later modern clipboard writes. Whole loaded-answer content must match, but native-copy coverage remains unverified and partial. No system clipboard readback supplies answer content.

The DOM reader requires explicit message IDs and does not invent parent IDs from visual order. It reads at most 200 message roots and marks a bounded or visibly truncated result as partial. Its scoped HTML retains headings, tables and code; KaTeX annotations retain their TeX source. Reasoning, tool/status regions and interactive controls are excluded. Internal native input uses the existing guest queue and rechecks the provider guard and actual click point immediately before dispatch.

The registered task service, native DeepSeek/Kimi/ChatGPT/Claude/Qwen/Doubao sessions and [task interface](../browser.md#ai-workspace) are connected in the production build. Local Electron fixtures verify three consecutive rounds per provider, Kimi and Doubao pagination, current-branch isolation, unfinished-status boundaries, stored Markdown, distinct repeated-question receipts, restart without resubmission, module disposal and responsive layouts. Qwen checks also cover Slate draft protection and localized provider names. HTTPS traffic is fulfilled locally during these checks. Real-account compatibility and acceptance remain unverified; these fixtures cannot establish the current website's private response or DOM contracts.
